issue_context.title: unclear `repl run` source environment
issue_context.body:
### Check for existing issues - [X] Completed ### Describe the bug / provide steps to reproduce it So I was trying to test some plot using `repl: run` around `python`. After setting up environment `pyrightconfig.json` with appropriate source python environment I tried to execute a simple code that uses `matplotlib`. Despite `matplotlib` being present in source environment I want to use that is defined in `pyrightconfig.json` the `repl` interpreter does not seem to recognize it delivering: ![Screenshot 2024-09-24 at 11 52 52 AM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1500f74-c992-4a2c-973a-676bbef1d57c) In short, please help me figure out how to source desired environment via `repl`. Thanks. PS. `repl: sessions` would show me all active kernels, just not sure how I can select the one of my liking? ![Screenshot 2024-09-24 at 11 58 46 AM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ee96f14-b091-44d0-a0a1-8e18ccab224c) and to repeat myself, the source env does have `matplotlib` installed, but the message show it isn't. ### Environment ``` Zed: v0.154.1 (Zed Preview) OS: macOS 15.0.0 Memory: 32 GiB Architecture: aarch64 ``` ### If applicable, add mockups / screenshots to help explain present your vision of the feature I expect ZED to recognize environment of my liking and be able to recognize underlying installed packages. ### If applicable, attach your Zed.log file to this issue.

Hmm.. how would it know where the `venvPath` is, regardless of what one uses `pyenv`/`poetry`/`uv` ? 🤔 

Right now I use in-project `pyrightconfig.json` such as:
```
{
  "venvPath": "/Users/<user>/.pyenv/versions",
  "venv": "my_virtual_env"
}
```
